Consult Summary:
- 26-year-old woman with three-day history of progressively worsening headache, diffuse with right-eye predominance, photophobia, neck stiffness, and difficulty focusing; not relieved by ibuprofen; family history of migraines; clinician suspects migraine-type headache and proposes stronger analgesia, trigger diary, and follow-up with discussion of preventive options.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Headache for ~3 days, described as dull overall with right-eye emphasis; intermittent worsening; currently severe (≈8/10).
- Onset/duration/progression: Began ~3 days ago at work; gradually worsened; present at all times with fluctuations; worse by morning after waking.
- Quality: Dull ache with episodes of sharper pain.
- Location: Headache felt all over, mainly around the right eye.
- Associated symptoms: Photophobia; light sensitivity; nausea without vomiting; neck stiffness; difficulty focusing; no reported vision loss or double vision; no fever or rashes.
- Aggravating/relieving factors: Ibuprofen used with limited relief; stress at work; screen brightness may contribute; hydration considered but not clearly implicated.
- Treatments tried: Ibuprofen (three tablets per day) for ~2 days; little to no relief.
- Past Medical History: Personal history of headaches; no prior migraine diagnosis; migraines in mother and sister.
- Allergies: None known.
- Medications: Ibuprofen (dose/route not documented; frequency reported as three times daily).
- Social History: Social smoker; social drinker; lives with three housemates; works in IT; uses glasses; increased screen exposure; reports work-related stress due to new project.
- Family History: Mother and sister with migraines; sister typically well-controlled, mother with migraines around seasonal changes.
- ROS: Notable for photophobia and neck stiffness; no visual loss, vomiting, fever, or rash documented beyond above.

Past Medical History:
- Headache history; no documented personal migraine diagnosis.
- Family history of migraines (mother and sister).

Medications:
- Ibuprofen — dose per tablet not documented; route not documented; frequency documented as three tablets daily.

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Smokes socially; drinks socially.
- Occupation: IT; frequent computer use; screens brightness reduced.
- Living situation: Four people in household (including patient).

Family History:
- Migraine: Mother and sister have migraines; variability in control.

Physical Examination:
- No vitals or objective physical examination findings documented.

Investigations:
- No investigations or test results documented.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1:
- Diagnosis/Impression: Probable migraine-type headache given clinical features and family history; not responding to NSAID therapy.
- Plan:
  - Optimize analgesia: 
    - Ibuprofen: discuss up to two tablets per dose, up to three times daily; dose per tablet not documented.
    - Consider alternative/additional analgesics if inadequate: Naproxen (dose/route/frequency not documented); Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented); Codeine (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Provide prescription today for stronger analgesic option(s) as discussed.
  - Headache diary: start documenting triggers, hydration, sleep, screens/work stress.
  - Follow-up: recheck in 1–2 weeks; if headaches become more frequent or persistent, discuss prophylactic therapy.
  - Red flags: return sooner if vision changes, weakness, or other concerning symptoms.

Issue 2:
- Ocular/photophobia management:
  - Reiterate the potential for ocular strain; recommend consideration of a repeat eye exam if symptoms persist or worsen; monitoring with reduced screen brightness as already practiced.

General Plan:
- Monitor response to new analgesic plan; adjust as needed.
- Provide patient education on migraine features and when to seek urgent care.

Quality checks:
- Missing elements:
  - Vitals and formal physical examination not provided.
  - No specific documented dosing/route for any prescribed medications beyond ibuprofen frequency; Naproxen/Paracetamol/Codeine doses not documented.
  - No imaging or laboratory results discussed.
  - Pregnancy status not documented (relevant for some analgesics) though not indicated by patient.
  - No explicit medication reconciliation beyond ibuprofen.
- Internal conflicts:
  - None identified in transcript.
- Transcript quality:
  - Some conversational noise and incomplete answers (e.g., question about on-the-pill status; no answer recorded).
  - Limited objective data (no vitals, no exam findings).
